subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit binding tiers miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source gap and security impact are clear, but changing fallback routing affects session state, provider/auth boundaries, and compatibility for existing Discord multi-account setups.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit bindings miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime fallback unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair the linked fork PR first
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after resolving conflicts, confirming the fallback contract, and adding real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit bindings miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history in shared routing, Discord route hardening, and prior maintainer-facing analysis for this issue.
